To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DOC concentrations measured in seawater are dependent on the type of DOC analyzer used (i.e., high-temperature catalytic oxidation (HTCO) or persulfate oxidation), the method used to prepare the sample for analysis (i.e., filtration, acidification, or acidification plus filtration), and the type of filter used for sample filtration (i.e., glass fiber, polycarbonate, or polytetrafluoroethylene).

the DOC concentration in seawater varies by a factor of 2 to 5, depending upon location and season; that DOC concentration is not related to salinity or to temperature; and that the DOC concentration varies from 0.5 to 1.5 mmol C/kg in the ocean.

the DOC concentration in seawater is not a constant, but varies with depth and location; that DOC is measured with an accuracy of 2-4%, but that the precision is 1-2% (depending on the sample); and that the DOC concentrations in seawater are not the same in all parts of the world.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of DOC and its relationship to the carbon cycle.
improving the measurement of DOC in seawater, especially in the open ocean.
the measurement of the quantity of DOC in seawater.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DOC problem remains unsolved.
there is no conclusive statement about DOC in seawater.
there are no simple answers to DOC measurement problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DOC concentration of seawater is a poorly defined quantity, and that the analytical methods used to measure it have a large impact on the results.
we are making progress in the effort to improve DOC measurements, but there is still much to do.
the DOC controversy is not over.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are not yet ready to make a statement on the accuracy of the DOC measurements made in the ocean.
there is no single method that can be used by all investigators to make DOC measurements.
the DOC problem is still with us and that we have a long way to go before we can be confident that we are measuring the same thing.
